fields.rationale: why the face keeps the shape it has — the work it does
fields.removal.lane: where the support body leaves and what it passes on the way out; null where no one has stated it yet
fields.removal.bench: what removing it took on a printed piece; null until one has been pulled

support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head square catch
support_bodies.rationale: The -X rail's broad, flat slide-head underside is the Z seam's one down-looking face on this floor-down piece. Lifting a seated back-top lands that piece's flat foot on this complete bearing plane. Its two interface islands are the one run either side of the required 12 mm PRV passage; that opening also lets the support body root on the bed outside the flank instead of on the arm's under-flare.

removal.lane: The groove under the catch is open air from the arm's sliding face out past the exterior plane. The body stands on the outside of the flank with a face exposed down the whole run, nothing over it and no branch turning back in. The PRV passage splits it in two, so it lifts off as two pieces.

support_bodies.name: west handhold lifting ceiling
support_bodies.rationale: The handhold keeps a flat bearing ceiling for upward finger contact, with 12 mm of roof section above it. This support reaches the back half of that ceiling from the print bed through the open bottom, with 34.40 mm of build-up.

removal.lane: The opening gives direct access to remove the complete body.

support_bodies.name: east handhold lifting ceiling

support_bodies.name: east Z-seam slide-head square catch
support_bodies.rationale: The +X rail's broad, flat slide-head underside mirrors the west one and remains continuous because nothing crosses this flank. With no opening through the wall beside it, the support has no lane to the bed and roots on the arm's own 45 degree under-flare 8.60 mm below the bearing plane.

removal.lane: The groove under the catch is open air from the arm's sliding face out past the exterior plane. The body stands on the outside of the flank with a face exposed down the whole run, nothing over it and no branch turning back in.

support_bodies.name: funnel brim seat, ASSE seats and pan berth, connector and identification pockets, west anchors and rail catches
support_bodies.rationale: The funnel brim bears on its recessed flat seat. The ASSE round seats, pan sleeve and berth, connector and identification pockets, anchor tie faces and rail catches retain their complete locating, retaining or bearing sections.

removal.lane: The connected branches are accessible through the funnel opening, open quadrant, pan openings and exposed rail grooves. Remove them before installing the funnel or internal hardware; the rail ribbons pull outward along the open flank grooves.

support_bodies.name: water-split anchor tie-band flank
support_bodies.rationale: The anchor keeps its round locating seat and the complete flank of its tie-band passage.

removal.lane: The tie passage opens into the empty quadrant; remove its support before placing the fitting and zip tie.

support_bodies.name: flow-regulator anchor tie-band flank

removal.lane: The tie cavity is open across the loose quadrant; remove the support before installing the ASSE assembly.

support_bodies.name: flow-regulator anchor tie-band crown
support_bodies.rationale: The flat crown bridges the regulator anchor tie-band passage without changing its locating seat.

removal.lane: The narrow support leaves through the open tie-band passage before the fitting and tie are installed.

support_bodies.name: west Z-seam slide-head square catch
support_bodies.rationale: The west rail keeps a broad flat bearing against lift along the top piece’s full foot. The support roots on the arm’s 45 degree under-flare, 8.00 mm below the catch. The lower and middle Y-seam passages have no separate support interface.

removal.lane: The groove under the catch is open air from the arm's sliding face out past the exterior plane. The body stands on the outside of the flank with a face exposed down the whole run, nothing over it and no branch turning back in.
removal.bench: Printed and pulled: among the easiest supports on the enclosure, off cleanly in one piece, reached from outside the flank without going near the cavity.
